[[File:Oi Jinja Kasama Torii.jpg|250px|thumb|<center>Torii</center>]]
'''Ōi Shrine''' (おおいじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in Kasama, Ibaraki, Ibaraki Prefecture. It is a Shikinaisha theoretical shrine and was formerly ranked as a village shrine under the Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines.

== Deity ==
* '''Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto'''

=== About the enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto, was a son of the first Emperor Jimmu and elder brother of the second Emperor Suizei. According to the Nihon Shoki, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto was the ancestor of the Tomo clan (descendants of Ōtomo). The Kojiki records him as the ancestor of nineteen clans, including the Ōomi, the Oko-be no Muraji, Sakaai-be no Muraji, Hi no Kimi, Ōita no Kimi, Aso no Kimi, Chikushi Mikeno Muraji, Suzume no Omi, Suzume no Miyatsuko, Onagaya no Miyatsuko, Tsuge no Naori, Iyokuni no Miyatsuko, Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Michinoku Ishijō no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Jōdō Naka no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Nagasa no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Ise Funaki no Naori, Owari Niwa no Omi, and Shimada no Omi.

Among these, the area near this shrine is thought to have been governed by the Nakakuni no Miyatsuko (Lord of Nakakuni), and it is believed that the shrine was established by the Nakakuni clan to worship their ancestor, Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto.

== History ==
=== Foundation ===
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was built in Daidō (Japan) 1 (806) by imperial decree at Watai-ga-mine in Ōi Village, Naka District, Hitachi Province, and was called Ōi Daimyōjin.

=== Outline of history ===
In the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, it is listed as "Ōi Shrine, Naka District, Hitachi Province," included among the Shikinaisha. In the Middle Ages, it was called "Tarō Myōjin" and revered as the general guardian shrine of the five villages of Fukuda, Iida, Ishidera, Terasaki, and Hizawa. Among the four shrines of Ōi, Hakoda, Ishii, and Kurusu, this shrine was regarded as the foremost and worshiped as "Ichinomiya Myōjin" (Shisho Ichinomiya).

== Grounds ==
The main hall (honden) was rebuilt in Meiwa 6 (1769). The sacred tree is a group of three cedar trees joined at the base, known as the "Parent and Child Cedars."

<gallery>
File:Oi Jinja Kasama Honden.jpg|Main Hall (Honden)
File:Oi Jinja Kasama Oyakosugi.jpg|Parent and Child Cedars (Sacred tree)
</gallery>

== Festivals ==
* New Year's Festival (January 1)
* Spring Festival (January 7)
* Setsubun Festival (February 3)
* Rice-Planting Festival (July 19)
* Autumn Festival (November 12)
